maya: Heads-up — ran a small int4 run on the llama2-13b -> mistral-8x conversion path, saw token mapping drift for emoji and zero-width joiners. Quick notes below.

carl: what quant toolchain? bitsandbytes/ggml/gguf int4?

maya: used our scripts/quantize.py -> gguf int4 (fused path), batch=8, seq_len=2048. Baseline FP16 vs int4 perplexity on wikitext+chat evals diverged only when inputs contained emoji + combining diacritics.

sophie: can you paste a couple delta examples?

maya: sure — repro pair below:

samp: "I love pizza 🍕‍🍳"  (rendered as pizza emoji + zwj + cook hat)

FP16 token ids: [1024, 789, 13001, 45213, 12]
INT4 token ids:  [1024, 789, 13001, 45214, 12]  <-- 45213 -> 45214 shift on ZWJ cluster

maya: dump from tokenizer:
```
>>> tok.encode("🍕‍🍳", nfkc=False)
[45213]
>>> tok.encode("🍕\u200d🍳", nfkc=True)
[45214]
```

ev an: hmm, that looks like normalization mismatch during conversion. Which tokenizer version & config did the convert job pin?

maya: llama-tokenizer v1.2, but convert pipeline used tokenizer.save() then reload on the target machine. I accidentally set nfkc=False in the conversion env; the original training tokenization was nfkc=True.

carl: that could explain token id mismatches. Also worth checking KV cache offsets — we've seen a separate bug where int4 kernel truncates rotary phase precision causing headwise wrap at large seq lengths.

sophie: do you have a small kv dump? paste head 0 angles hex.

maya: kv hex (first 3 k vectors head0):
```
fp16 head0 k[0:3]: [0x3fe0a2b3, 0x3fd123ff, 0x3fc88a10]
int4 head0 k[0:3]: [0x3fe0a2b2, 0x3fd123e0, 0x3fc88a00]
``` 
subtle shifts on LSBs, might nudge rotary when combining with off-by-one token id.

ev an: action items to triage:
1) re-run encoding with nfkc=True on the source and target and assert token id parity
2) run fp16 vs int4 forward with identical token ids and diff logits to see if quant introduces rotary wrap
3) if mismatch persists, reproduce minimal test and open quant kernel issue

maya: running (1)-(2) now. preliminary: forcing nfkc=True fixes token id parity. Re-ran int4 forward with same ids and still saw tiny logit drift for the emoji cluster -> likely rotary precision + embed proj ordering interaction.

carl: remember the gemma conversion patch last quarter where embed_proj order got reversed; that gave subtle phase misalign. Could be same class.

sophie: let's add a small conversion check in the pipeline: after tokenize+normalize run a checksum (sha256) of normalized codepoints and compare source->converted vocab; fail converter on mismatch. Also add an onboarding unit test for emoji + ZWJ clusters.

maya: opened PR with repro and nfkc toggle: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2145 — includes test in tests/onboard/repro_emoji_zwj.py and a docstring explaining nfkc.

infra-bot: Conversion job 4821 completed for artifact gs://redwood-models/conv/1762/llama2-13b-gguf->mistral-8x-gguf. Logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/logs/conv-4821

infra-bot: CI for PR #2145 started: 8 jobs queued.

infra-bot: CI job quant-e2e failed on container bench step (exit 137) — full log: https://ci.redwood.dev/jobs/9987

ev an: I'll pick up the quant-e2e failure. suspect exporter zero-padding in gguf int4 path. assigning to @evan.

carl: short-term mitigation: add a conversion fallback to force fp16 for models with high emoji fraction (>0.5% tokens) or inject prefix caching for those routes to avoid hitting the drift in production.

sophie: long-term, add post-convert tokenization checksum + rotary sanity (compare phase angles on a few probe tokens). If checksum fails, mark conversion as review_required.

maya: ack. I'll add checksum step in convert script and attach to PR #2145. Also adding a tiny repro dataset with emoji/ZWJ clusters to onboarding suite.

ev an: update — reproduced kernel truncation locally in quant bench; debugging quant packer now. Will post patch by EOD.

maya: thanks team. next status in thread when infra CI updates. :coffee:
